## Overview

Combines the exports of `04` (KEGG pathway membership) and `05` (STRING GO Biological Process enrichment on the whole curated gene set) into one table of (`spatial_pair`, gene, function), and summarises which functions each cell-type pair's significant LR genes point to.

Outputs:

- `function_convergence` -- every function, with how many `spatial_pair`s and genes hit it;
- `pair_summary` -- top functions per `spatial_pair`;
- a heatmap of `spatial_pair` x function, for functions shared by 2+ pairs that are concentrated in one or a few of them.

Run `04` and `05` first.

```{r setup}
library(dplyr)
library(tibble)
library(ggplot2)
```

## Load exports

```{r load-exports}
kegg_gene_pathway     <- read.csv(file.path("output", "04_KEGG_PathwayConvergence", "kegg_gene_pathway_by_pair.csv"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
string_enrichment_all <- read.csv(file.path("output", "05_STRING_NetworkAnalysis", "string_whole_network_enrichment.csv"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
```

`spatial_pair` per gene is rebuilt from `significant_lr_pairs.csv`.

```{r rebuild-lr-genes-long}
split_complex <- function(x) stringr::str_split(x, "_")

sig_pairs <- read.csv(file.path("output", "03c_crossModality_plots", "significant_lr_pairs.csv"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE) %>%
  distinct(spatial_pair, ligand_complex, receptor_complex)

lr_gene_sets <- purrr::pmap(sig_pairs, function(spatial_pair, ligand_complex, receptor_complex) {
  ligands   <- unlist(split_complex(ligand_complex))
  receptors <- unlist(split_complex(receptor_complex))
  tibble(spatial_pair = spatial_pair, gene = unique(c(ligands, receptors)))
})

lr_genes_long <- bind_rows(lr_gene_sets) %>% distinct(spatial_pair, gene)
lr_genes_long
```

## STRING GO Biological Process membership

GO Biological Process terms from the STRING enrichment, with the genes supporting each term.

```{r string-process-membership}
fdr_col   <- intersect(c("fdr", "false_discovery_rate", "p_value"), names(string_enrichment_all))[1]
cat_col   <- intersect(c("category"), names(string_enrichment_all))[1]
desc_col  <- intersect(c("description"), names(string_enrichment_all))[1]
term_col  <- intersect(c("term"), names(string_enrichment_all))[1]
genes_col <- intersect(c("preferredNames", "inputGenes", "genes"), names(string_enrichment_all))[1]

if (is.na(cat_col) || is.na(genes_col) || is.na(term_col) || is.na(desc_col)) {
  stop("Couldn't find the expected columns in string_whole_network_enrichment.csv. ",
       "Columns present: ", paste(names(string_enrichment_all), collapse = ", "))
}

string_process_gene <- string_enrichment_all %>%
  dplyr::filter(.data[[cat_col]] == "Process") %>%
  transmute(
    function_id   = .data[[term_col]],
    function_name = .data[[desc_col]],
    fdr           = .data[[fdr_col]],
    gene          = stringr::str_split(.data[[genes_col]], ",\\s*")
  ) %>%
  tidyr::unnest(gene) %>%
  distinct(function_id, function_name, gene)

string_process_gene
```

## Drop overly generic GO terms

Broad terms near the top of the GO hierarchy ("regulation of cellular process") are enriched in almost any gene set. Terms with more than `max_background_genes` genes genome-wide are removed.

```{r string-specificity-filter}
bg_col <- intersect(
  c("number_of_genes_in_background", "background_gene_count", "bgCount", "genesInBackground"),
  names(string_enrichment_all)
)[1]

if (is.na(bg_col)) {

  message("No genome-wide background-size column found -- specificity filter skipped.")

} else {

  process_bg <- string_enrichment_all %>%
    dplyr::filter(.data[[cat_col]] == "Process") %>%
    dplyr::transmute(function_id = .data[[term_col]], background_size = .data[[bg_col]])

  max_background_genes <- 300   # lower = only more specific terms survive

  q <- stats::quantile(process_bg$background_size, probs = c(0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1))
  n_before <- dplyr::n_distinct(process_bg$function_id)
  keep_ids <- process_bg %>% dplyr::filter(background_size <= max_background_genes) %>% dplyr::pull(function_id)
  n_after  <- length(unique(keep_ids))

  message(
    "Term size quantiles (", n_before, " terms): ",
    paste(names(q), q, sep = " = ", collapse = ", "),
    ". Keeping <= ", max_background_genes, " genes: ", n_after, " of ", n_before, " terms."
  )

  string_process_gene <- string_process_gene %>% dplyr::filter(function_id %in% keep_ids)
}

string_process_gene
```

## Collapse STRING terms with identical gene evidence

Nested GO terms ("regulation of X", "positive regulation of X") are often supported by exactly the same genes. Terms with an identical set of `spatial_pair`:gene evidence are merged into one row, named after the shortest term.

```{r string-collapse}
string_gene_level <- string_process_gene %>%
  inner_join(lr_genes_long, by = "gene", relationship = "many-to-many") %>%
  distinct(spatial_pair, gene, function_id, function_name)

string_signature <- string_gene_level %>%
  mutate(evidence = paste0(spatial_pair, ":", gene)) %>%
  group_by(function_id, function_name) %>%
  summarise(signature = paste(sort(unique(evidence)), collapse = "|"), .groups = "drop")

string_signature_groups <- string_signature %>%
  group_by(signature) %>%
  summarise(
    n_terms              = n(),
    term_names           = paste(sort(function_name), collapse = "; "),
    representative_id    = function_id[which.min(nchar(function_name))],
    representative_name  = function_name[which.min(nchar(function_name))],
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(n_terms))

string_id_to_group <- string_signature %>%
  left_join(
    string_signature_groups %>% dplyr::select(signature, representative_id, representative_name, n_terms),
    by = "signature"
  )

string_signature_groups %>% dplyr::select(representative_name, n_terms, term_names)
```

## Reduce STRING terms by semantic similarity (rrvgo)

Merges GO terms that are closely related in the GO graph even if their genes differ slightly (`rrvgo`, the method behind REVIGO). The most significant term (lowest FDR) names each group. Needs `rrvgo`, `GOSemSim` and `org.Mm.eg.db`.

```{r string-semantic-reduce}
if (!requireNamespace("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("BiocManager")
for (pkg in c("rrvgo", "GOSemSim", "org.Mm.eg.db")) {
  if (!requireNamespace(pkg, quietly = TRUE)) BiocManager::install(pkg, update = FALSE, ask = FALSE)
}

rep_terms <- string_signature_groups %>% dplyr::distinct(representative_id, representative_name)

# -log10(FDR): higher score = preferred as group label
term_fdr <- string_enrichment_all %>%
  dplyr::filter(.data[[cat_col]] == "Process") %>%
  dplyr::transmute(function_id = .data[[term_col]], fdr = .data[[fdr_col]])

scores <- term_fdr$fdr[match(rep_terms$representative_id, term_fdr$function_id)]
scores <- setNames(-log10(pmax(scores, 1e-300)), rep_terms$representative_id)

simMatrix <- rrvgo::calculateSimMatrix(
  rep_terms$representative_id,
  orgdb  = "org.Mm.eg.db",
  ont    = "BP",
  method = "Rel"
)

semantic_similarity_threshold <- 0.7   # rrvgo: 0.9 large, 0.7 medium, 0.5 small, 0.4 tiny groups

reduced_terms <- rrvgo::reduceSimMatrix(
  simMatrix,
  scores[rownames(simMatrix)],
  threshold = semantic_similarity_threshold,
  orgdb     = "org.Mm.eg.db"
)

string_semantic_group <- tibble::as_tibble(reduced_terms) %>%
  dplyr::transmute(representative_id = go, semantic_parent_id = parent, semantic_parent_name = parentTerm)

# every raw GO term now maps to one final group (identical-evidence + semantic merging)
string_id_to_group <- string_id_to_group %>%
  dplyr::left_join(string_semantic_group, by = "representative_id") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    final_id   = dplyr::coalesce(semantic_parent_id, representative_id),
    final_name = dplyr::coalesce(semantic_parent_name, representative_name)
  )

final_group_sizes <- string_id_to_group %>% dplyr::count(final_id, name = "n_terms_final")

string_id_to_group <- string_id_to_group %>%
  dplyr::select(-n_terms) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(final_group_sizes, by = "final_id") %>%
  dplyr::rename(n_terms = n_terms_final)

string_id_to_group %>%
  dplyr::distinct(final_name, n_terms) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(n_terms))
```

## Collapse KEGG pathways with identical gene evidence

Hub genes sit in dozens of KEGG maps, many of them disease or infection maps, so the same few genes repeat across many pathways. Pathways with identical `spatial_pair`:gene evidence are merged into one row.

```{r kegg-collapse}
kegg_gene_level <- kegg_gene_pathway %>%
  distinct(spatial_pair, gene, pathway_id, pathway_name)

kegg_signature <- kegg_gene_level %>%
  mutate(evidence = paste0(spatial_pair, ":", gene)) %>%
  group_by(pathway_id, pathway_name) %>%
  summarise(signature = paste(sort(unique(evidence)), collapse = "|"), .groups = "drop")

kegg_signature_groups <- kegg_signature %>%
  group_by(signature) %>%
  summarise(
    n_pathways           = n(),
    pathway_names        = paste(sort(pathway_name), collapse = "; "),
    representative_id    = pathway_id[which.min(nchar(pathway_name))],
    representative_name  = pathway_name[which.min(nchar(pathway_name))],
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(n_pathways))

kegg_id_to_group <- kegg_signature %>%
  left_join(
    kegg_signature_groups %>% dplyr::select(signature, representative_id, representative_name, n_pathways),
    by = "signature"
  )

kegg_signature_groups %>% dplyr::select(representative_name, n_pathways, pathway_names)
```

## Combined (spatial_pair, gene, function) table

Merged groups are labelled "name (+N more)".

```{r combine}
kegg_long <- kegg_gene_level %>%
  left_join(
    kegg_id_to_group %>% dplyr::select(pathway_id, representative_id, representative_name, n_pathways),
    by = "pathway_id"
  ) %>%
  transmute(
    function_source = "KEGG pathway",
    function_id     = representative_id,
    function_name   = if_else(
      n_pathways > 1,
      paste0(representative_name, " (+", n_pathways - 1, " more)"),
      representative_name
    ),
    spatial_pair,
    gene
  ) %>%
  distinct()

string_long <- string_gene_level %>%
  left_join(
    string_id_to_group %>% dplyr::select(function_id, final_id, final_name, n_terms),
    by = "function_id"
  ) %>%
  transmute(
    function_source = "STRING: Biological Process",
    function_id     = final_id,
    function_name   = if_else(
      n_terms > 1,
      paste0(final_name, " (+", n_terms - 1, " more)"),
      final_name
    ),
    spatial_pair,
    gene
  ) %>%
  distinct()

function_by_pair_long <- bind_rows(kegg_long, string_long)
function_by_pair_long
```

## Function-level convergence

```{r function-convergence}
function_convergence <- function_by_pair_long %>%
  distinct(function_source, function_id, function_name, spatial_pair, gene) %>%
  group_by(function_source, function_id, function_name) %>%
  summarise(
    n_spatial_pairs_hitting_it = n_distinct(spatial_pair),
    n_distinct_genes           = n_distinct(gene),
    spatial_pairs               = paste(sort(unique(spatial_pair)), collapse = ", "),
    genes                       = paste(sort(unique(gene)), collapse = ", "),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(n_spatial_pairs_hitting_it), desc(n_distinct_genes))

# function_name is not unique (a KEGG name can equal a STRING description), so build a
# unique display label: "KEGG: ..." / "STRING: ...", plus the id if still duplicated
name_collisions <- function_convergence %>% dplyr::count(function_name) %>% dplyr::filter(n > 1)
if (nrow(name_collisions) > 0) {
  message(nrow(name_collisions), " function_name value(s) shared by more than one function_id: ",
          paste(name_collisions$function_name, collapse = "; "))
}

function_labels <- function_convergence %>%
  dplyr::distinct(function_id, function_name, function_source) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    source_prefix = dplyr::case_when(
      function_source == "KEGG pathway"                ~ "KEGG: ",
      function_source == "STRING: Biological Process"  ~ "STRING: ",
      TRUE                                              ~ paste0(function_source, ": ")
    ),
    function_label = paste0(source_prefix, function_name)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(function_label) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(function_label = if (dplyr::n() > 1) paste0(function_label, " [", function_id, "]") else function_label) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::select(function_id, function_label)

function_convergence <- function_convergence %>%
  dplyr::left_join(function_labels, by = "function_id")

function_convergence
```

## Per-spatial-pair summary

Number of functions per pair, and its top 3 functions (most shared across pairs first).

```{r pair-summary}
pair_function_ranked <- function_by_pair_long %>%
  distinct(spatial_pair, function_source, function_id, function_name) %>%
  left_join(
    function_convergence %>% dplyr::select(function_id, function_label, n_spatial_pairs_hitting_it, n_distinct_genes),
    by = "function_id"
  ) %>%
  arrange(spatial_pair, desc(n_spatial_pairs_hitting_it), desc(n_distinct_genes), function_label)

pair_summary <- pair_function_ranked %>%
  group_by(spatial_pair) %>%
  summarise(
    n_kegg_pathways        = n_distinct(function_id[function_source == "KEGG pathway"]),
    n_string_bio_processes = n_distinct(function_id[function_source == "STRING: Biological Process"]),
    top_functions          = paste(head(function_label, 3), collapse = "; "),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

pair_summary
```

## Specificity of each function, corrected for gene-pool size

Pairs can have very different numbers of genes, so raw gene counts favour large pairs. For each function, each pair's **coverage** (its genes on the function / its total genes) is computed first, and `specificity_score` is that pair's share of the summed coverage. Contributions of a single gene are dropped.

```{r pair-gene-pools}
pair_gene_pool_size <- lr_genes_long %>% dplyr::count(spatial_pair, name = "pool_size")
pair_gene_pool_size
```

```{r specificity}
pair_function_specificity <- function_by_pair_long %>%
  distinct(function_source, function_id, function_name, spatial_pair, gene) %>%
  group_by(function_source, function_id, function_name, spatial_pair) %>%
  summarise(n_genes = n_distinct(gene), .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(n_genes > 1) %>%   # drop single-gene contributions before computing shares
  left_join(pair_gene_pool_size, by = "spatial_pair") %>%
  mutate(pair_coverage = n_genes / pool_size) %>%
  group_by(function_id) %>%
  mutate(
    total_genes_all_pairs = sum(n_genes),
    raw_gene_share        = n_genes / total_genes_all_pairs,     # uncorrected, for reference
    specificity_score     = pair_coverage / sum(pair_coverage)   # pool-size-corrected share
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  left_join(function_labels, by = "function_id") %>%
  arrange(desc(n_genes), desc(specificity_score))

pair_function_specificity
```

### Keep functions that differ between pairs

Functions split evenly across pairs say little. `specificity_range` (max − min `specificity_score` across contributing pairs) must be at least `min_specificity_range`; functions with a single contributing pair count as fully specific.

```{r specificity-spread}
function_specificity_spread <- pair_function_specificity %>%
  group_by(function_id) %>%
  summarise(
    n_pairs_contributing = dplyr::n(),
    specificity_range    = if (dplyr::n() > 1) max(specificity_score) - min(specificity_score) else 1,
    .groups = "drop"
  )

min_specificity_range <- 0.3   # 0 = keep all; higher = only functions concentrated in one pair

differential_ids <- function_specificity_spread %>%
  dplyr::filter(specificity_range >= min_specificity_range) %>%
  dplyr::pull(function_id)

message(length(differential_ids), " of ", nrow(function_specificity_spread),
        " functions pass the spread cutoff (>= ", min_specificity_range, ").")

function_specificity_spread %>% dplyr::arrange(desc(specificity_range))
```

## Heatmap: spatial_pair x function

Functions hit by 2+ pairs that pass the spread filter. Colour and percentage = `specificity_score`; number in brackets = genes.

```{r heatmap-data}
# column order; a pair left out here is only hidden from the plot
spatial_pair_order <- c("Astrocyte-Vascular", "Vascular-Microglia",
                         "OPC-Cajal.Retzius", "Neurogenic_lineage-GC")

convergent_ids <- function_convergence %>%
  filter(n_spatial_pairs_hitting_it >= 2, function_id %in% differential_ids) %>%
  pull(function_id)

heatmap_data <- function_by_pair_long %>%
  filter(function_id %in% convergent_ids) %>%
  distinct(spatial_pair, function_id, gene) %>%
  group_by(spatial_pair, function_id) %>%
  summarise(n_genes = n_distinct(gene), .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(n_genes > 1) %>%
  left_join(function_labels, by = "function_id")

# rows ordered by convergence, most-shared first
function_order <- function_convergence %>%
  filter(function_id %in% unique(heatmap_data$function_id)) %>%
  arrange(desc(n_spatial_pairs_hitting_it), desc(n_distinct_genes)) %>%
  pull(function_label)

heatmap_data <- heatmap_data %>%
  mutate(function_label = factor(function_label, levels = rev(function_order)))
```

```{r specificity-heatmap}
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 9

specificity_heatmap_data <- pair_function_specificity %>%
  filter(function_id %in% unique(heatmap_data$function_id)) %>%
  mutate(function_label = factor(function_label, levels = rev(function_order)))

ggplot(specificity_heatmap_data, aes(x = spatial_pair, y = function_label, fill = specificity_score)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "#fcfcfb", linewidth = 2) +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(scales::percent(specificity_score, accuracy = 1), " (", n_genes, ")"),
                colour = specificity_score > 0.6), size = 3, show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_fill_gradientn(colours = c("#cde2fb", "#6da7ec", "#2a78d6", "#0d366b"),
                        limits = c(0, 1), name = "Share of\nevidence") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "#fcfcfb", `FALSE` = "#0b0b0b")) +
  scale_x_discrete(position = "top", limits = spatial_pair_order) +
  scale_y_discrete(labels = scales::label_wrap(45)) +   # wrap long term names
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, title = "Evidence specificity by spatial pair") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    panel.grid  = element_blank(),
    axis.text.x = element_text(face = "bold", angle = 30, hjust = 0, vjust = 0),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8),
    plot.title  = element_text(margin = margin(b = 10)),
    plot.background  = element_rect(fill = "#fcfcfb", colour = NA),
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "#fcfcfb", colour = NA)
  )
```

## Notes on interpretation

- `specificity_score` describes how the evidence for a function is distributed across pairs; it is not a significance test. With 2–3 genes per cell, one gene changes it a lot, so read it together with `n_genes`.
- A function shared by 2+ pairs means their genes implicate the same broader biology, not that the LR pairs interact with each other.
- KEGG membership (curated, no test) and STRING GO enrichment (over-representation test on the whole gene set) are different kinds of evidence; a function supported by both is stronger. Genes with weak enrichment signal can be missing from the STRING side.
- "(+N more)" rows are merged terms: see `kegg_signature_groups`, `string_signature_groups` and `string_id_to_group` for what was merged.
- The heatmap is a display filter only; `function_convergence` and `pair_function_specificity` contain every function.
